newsitem.title: USA: Housing starts down in May for third straight month.
newsitem.headline: Housing starts down in May for third straight month.

text.p: Construction starts on new homes and apartments dropped for a third consecutive month in May, the Commerce Department said on Tuesday, as the housing sector gradually lost some strength.

Total starts fell 4.8 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.397 million in May after revised declines of 0.7 percent in April and 4.8 percent in March. The figures still suggest a relatively solid housing market, supported by a steadily expanding economy, although building is expected to decline gradually in coming months from a boom pace at the beginning of the year.
